ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and periodically thereafter, screen all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, UBOs, intermediaries, banks and material counterparties against United Nations Security Council sanctions, European Union restrictive-measures lists, Spanish domestic sanctions and terrorism-financing measures, OFAC SDN and other relevant OFAC lists, UK sanctions where commercially relevant, adverse media, criminal or regulatory enforcement sources, and politically exposed person databases. Apply Law 10/2010 risk-based customer due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, enhanced due diligence for PEPs, high-risk countries, opaque ownership, nominee arrangements, unusual payment routes and high-risk medical-device transactions. Retain due-diligence records for the statutory period, generally ten years under Law 10/2010. Do not treat an OFAC listing as automatically binding Spanish law, but assess it as a material correspondent-bank, export-control and contractual risk.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central, official portal: https://www.rmc.es; incorporation may also be coordinated through the CIRCE system and a Punto de Atención al Emprendedor where eligible
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be unique and distinguishable in the Central Commercial Registry and must include or correspond to the legal-form designation Sociedad Limitada, Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, S.L. or S.R.L. Names may use Latin characters and accepted Spanish orthography. Foreign or transliterated terms are generally permissible if they are not misleading, unlawful or confusingly similar to an existing name. The name does not replace any required regulated-sector authorization or trademark clearance. A separate trademark search at the Spanish Patent and Trademark Office and, where relevant, EUIPO is required.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms suggesting banking, insurance, securities, public authority, regulated healthcare status or official certification without the corresponding authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File the name-clearance application with the Registro Mercantil Central, submit up to five proposed names in priority order, and pay the applicable registry fee. The certificate of denominación social is generally valid for three months from issuance for incorporation purposes; the underlying reservation may be renewable in accordance with registry rules, and a new certificate should be obtained if the incorporation deadline is missed. Upon rejection, obtain the written registry reason, review similarity, prohibited-term and legal-form grounds, correct the proposal, and submit a new application. If the applicant contests a registrarial qualification, file a written appeal with the Commercial Registry within the statutory period, generally one month from notification under the Commercial Registry Regulation, or request a substitute review where legally available. A subsequent appeal may be made to the Directorate-General for Legal Certainty and Public Faith, without prejudice to judicial review. Registry-name approval does not eliminate trademark, unfair-competition or sector-licensing risk.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Spanish SL must have a registered office in Spain under the Companies Act and the registered office must correspond to the effective center of administration or principal establishment within the statutory rules. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for registration, mail handling and limited administrative functions if the provider permits use of the address and the company maintains reliable access to records and official communications. For manufacture of in-vitro diagnostic medical devices, a purely virtual office is not commercially or regulatorily adequate. The company should maintain suitable premises, quality-management records, technical documentation, complaint and vigilance systems, responsible personnel, storage and production arrangements, and evidence of operational control. Applicable principal instruments include Regulation (EU) 2017/746 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices, Regulation (EU) 2017/745 where relevant, Spanish Royal Decree 192/2023 of 21 March on medical devices, and AEMPS requirements. The manufacturer may require AEMPS registration or notification, conformity assessment, CE marking, an EU declaration of conformity, a quality-management system, notified-body involvement for applicable IVD classes, post-market surveillance and vigilance procedures.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official national probability is published. Qualitative risk is medium to high for this activity because it involves regulated IVD manufacturing, product-safety obligations, AEMPS oversight, quality systems and potential notified-body audits. For internal planning only, an estimated 10-20 percent annual probability of an unannounced or short-notice regulatory, tax, customs or labor-related site visit may be used; this is not a statutory statistic and may materially increase following complaints, adverse incidents, import irregularities, licensing gaps, inconsistent registry data or high-risk AML indicators.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July (Consolidated Text of the Spanish Companies Act, Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 20-22, 23, 55-58 and 61-64; Law 18/2022 on Business Creation and Growth (Ley Crea y Crece) for single-document electronic incorporation; Commercial Code Article 119.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for the negative name certificate and provincial Registro Mercantil of the registered office for final statutory registration; notarization by a Notary of the competent Colegio Notarial.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) filed electronically through the Documento Único Electrónico (DUE) portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SL requires minimum paid-up capital of EUR 3,000 (approximately USD 3,250), fully subscribed and fully paid in at incorporation; capital must be evidenced by a Spanish bank deposit certificate or, under Ley Crea y Crece, by a notarial payment certificate; no state escrow is required, but the capital cannot be withdrawn until the deed is registered.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: that the founding members, having subscribed and paid in full the share capital deposited into the company's provisional bank account, ratify the Escritura Pública de Constitución executed before the Notary. RESOLVED SECOND: that the registered office of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is fixed at the licensed manufacturing address stated in the deed. RESOLVED THIRD: that [Name] is appointed Administrador Único with all powers granted by the Companies Act, including banking, tax, AEMPS industrial licensing, and employment registrations. RESOLVED FOURTH: that the administrator is authorized to engage a certified occupational risk prevention service and an environmental consultant. RESOLVED FIFTH: that the administrator shall complete commercial registration, definitive NIF issuance, and municipal opening licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (via CIRCE or Registradores.es portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation request for the proposed SL denomination; the registry verifies that the name does not conflict with existing or protected business names and issues the Certificación Negativa de la Denominación Social within three business days; tender the original certificate to the Notary at deed execution.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Shareholders' NIE or passport copies
Power of attorney of the incorporator if signed by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is refused, submit up to three alternative names in one re-application; a new certificate is ordinarily issued within 24 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Minimum Share Capital and Obtain Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution authorized by Banco de España; alternative notarial payment certificate under Ley Crea y Crece
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the name of the intended SL and deposit the minimum EUR 3,000 paid-up capital; request the bank's Certificado de Desembolso stating the exact corporate name, account number, amount and deposit date; preserve the certificate for notarial delivery.
required_dossiers: Corporate purpose draft
Provisional company name certificate
Shareholders' identification documents
Account opening application and anti-money-laundering questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues an incomplete certificate, request a corrected certificate re-stating the exact SL denomination and paid-in amount; refrain from making withdrawals before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed of Incorporation Before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the Colegio Notarial competent at the incorporation location
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the name certificate, capital deposit certificate, final draft Bylaws (Estatutos), and fiscal identification of shareholders; the Notary reads, authenticates and seals the Escritura Pública de Constitución, including the corporate purpose for IVD manufacturing and appointment of the Administrador Único; obtain the first copy and urgent registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificación Negativa de la Denominación Social
Bank or notarial capital deposit certificate
Bylaws (Estatutos)
NIE/passport and fiscal identification of shareholders
Ley Crea y Crece DUE service request where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary raises defects, correct the deficient items (e.g., NIE numbers, addresses, signatory capacity) and schedule a new notarial appointment; notarial fees are preserved if the appointment is postponed more than five working days in advance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File and Self-Assess Capital Transfer and Documented Legal Acts Tax (ITP-AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional tax office (Dirección General de Tributos / Agencia Tributaria of the Autonomous Community)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Self-assess the AJD tax on the SL constitution within 30 business days from the deed date on the regional Model 600 form; pay online through the autonomous community tax portal or at an associate bank; keep the stamped and receipted form, which is mandatory for commercial registration.
required_dossiers: Signed copy of the public deed
Model 600 / regional AJD self-assessment form
NIE/NIF of the legal representative if paid by proxy
Proof of payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the regional office disputes the calculation, file a complementary declaration with proof of payment and the deed, or remedy the self-assessment through the regional economic-administrative rectification procedure before surcharge accrues.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Deed at the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original deed, AJD payment receipt and application through the DUE electronic filing service; the Registrar verifies legality and identity and, upon approval, confers legal personality and the corporate registration certificate required for all follow-up public licenses.
required_dossiers: Original Escritura Pública with AJD tax stamp
Model 036 census application
Registry tariff payment receipt
Identity documents of the appointed administrator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a defect note (nota de defecto), the Notary must sign a supplementary certificate correcting the observed variance and the deed must be re-submitted within the legal term without losing registration priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Definitive Tax Identification Number (NIF) and Register with Social Security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of registry registration, file Form 036/037 with AEAT to obtain the definitive NIF, register the SL in the Census of Obliged Taxpayers, elect the IAE activity group for IVD manufacturing, and open the employer's Social Security contribution account at TGSS, simultaneously enrolling the administrator under the RETA special regime.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration issued by Registro Mercantil
Public deed of incorporation
Form 036/037 census declaration
Identity document and power of attorney
Employer registration form TA.6 and RETA affiliation form TA.0521
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF is delayed, the SL may operate provisionally with the provisional NIF code; correct any mismatch between the deed, registry certificate and shareholder identification through a new Form 036 correction filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: AEMPS (Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios), Ministry of Health, together with the autonomous community health authority for manufacturing establishments
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización Sanitaria del Establecimiento de Fabricación de Productos Sanitarios para Diagnóstico in Vitro, combined with municipal Licencia de Actividad / Licencia de Apertura for the manufacturing plant

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Dirección General de Calidad Ambiental of the Autonomous Community and the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (MITERD)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Simplified Environmental Impact Assessment (Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Simplificada) under Annex II of Law 21/2013 for medium-scale manufacture of healthcare reagents; smaller plants located in an industrial estate may instead be covered by the municipal environmental license (Licencia Ambiental) if they fall below the EIA threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater must comply with the municipal industrial discharge ordinance: pH 5.5-9.5, BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, COD ≤ 500 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L, fats and oils ≤ 15 mg/L; solvent-containing immunoassay reagent processes are subject to Royal Decree 117/2003 on VOC emission limits, triggering a solvent management plan when annual solvent consumption exceeds 5 tonnes; biological and chemical residues from microfluidic cartridges must be inactivated, segregated and transferred to an authorized waste manager under Law 7/2022 on waste and contaminated soils, with ADR transport manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate of conformity with CTE DB-SI and final inspection by the regional fire brigade; structural load verification for the cleanroom raised floor and heavy immunoassay analyzers; municipal legalization report proving compliance with urban planning, accessibility and public safety requirements; occupational risk prevention clearance under Law 31/1995, covering chemical, biological, ergonomic and physical risks, and laboratory biosafety evaluation under Royal Decree 448/2020, including ventilation, emergency evacuation, PPE and periodic occupational health surveillance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); e-office portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es (Sede Electrónica), with electronic filing via form 036/037 and SII web services
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish SL obtains its definitive NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) from the AEAT Delegación de Grandes Contribuyentes or the local Provincia de Hacienda: (1) obtain a negative name-certificate (certificación negativa de denominación) from the Registro Mercantil Central; (2) execute the incorporation deed (escritura pública) before a notary; (3) obtain a provisional NIF (NIF provisional); (4) file the deed at the Registro Mercantil within two months; (5) apply for the definitive NIF on form 036 within one month of registration; (6) register for IAE (Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas) and VAT on form 036/037. A non-resident owner without Spanish presence must appoint a tax representative (representante fiscal) in Spain where required by Article 45.3 Ley 58/2003 (e.g., for large-net-worth or specific non-established operations) and apply for an NIF for the foreign entity on form 036 before commencing any Spanish taxable activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is a resident corporate taxpayer under Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS); general CIT rate 25%; branch of a non-Spanish EU entity is taxed at a 61.2% effective corporate rate under the branch-matching rule where applicable, except treaty override). Territorial scope: worldwide income of Spanish-resident SL, subject to participation exemption (ART. 21 LIS) and CFC rules (ART. 100-108 LIS); non-resident passive income may be covered by the Transparencia Fiscal Internacional regime. Tax-Exempt Zone status: not applicable, except reduced IS rates and ZEC (Zona Especial Canaria) regime for Canary Islands operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain is a civil-law unitary system without US-style check-the-box elections. Available statutory elections include: (i) reduced IS rate elections for newly created SLs (25% on first 300,000 EUR for small entities (type 26)); (ii) the ETVE (Entidad de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros) international holding regime under ART. 21 LIS with tax treaty network, which may be elected for inbound portfolio dividends; (iii) the Spanish patent box regime (ART. 23 LIS) reduced rate election for qualifying intangible income from R&D-derived assets; (iv) the indirect attribution of VAT groupings (grupo de IVA / VAT group in Spain); (v) the special deemed- attribution for permanent establishments of non-residents (ART. 22.2 LIS) for importing foreign-law transparent entities into the Spanish PE — combined with EU anti-hybrid rules (Directive 2016/1164 and Ley 27/2014) that disallow BEPS hybrid mismatches at the level of a Spanish SL receiving interest/royalties from a hybrid-payor jurisdiction; (vi) optional IS installment elections (payment options under ART. 40.3 LIS).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish Value Added Tax) under Ley 37/1992 and Real Decreto 1624/1992; harmonized with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; fiscal representation for non-established traders; IOSS/OSS one-stop-shop schemes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis threshold for an established Spanish SL (registration is compulsory from the first taxable supply of goods/services in Spanish territory). For intra-community distance sales of goods and telecommunications/broadcasting/e-services (except for the OSS 'one-stop-shop' scheme), the EU-wide distance-selling threshold of EUR 10,000 (VAT turnover) triggers Spanish VAT liability; non-established remote sellers must register through the OSS-IOSS scheme for imports of consignments not exceeding EUR 150, and otherwise via form 036/037 direct registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) real-time/VAT book clearance for taxpayers in REDEME (large companies with turnover > EUR 6,010,121.04), for monthly self-assessment schemes, or those in the simplified/agricultural/reinsurance special regimes; SII requires the registering/logging of all customer/supplier invoices into the AEAT e-office through XML via HTTPS web-services/API within 4 business days (max 8 calendar days) of issue or receipt (invoice record). Aggregated periodical returns (modelo 303 monthly or quarterly and modelo 349/390) remain due. For B2G invoicing to Spanish public administrations, the Facturae XML standard and the General Entry Point (Punto General de Entrada de Facturas, FACe) are mandatory. Additionally, under Law 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece), electronic invoicing (Facturae format or interoperable European EN 16931 formats) becomes mandatory for all B2B invoices between firms with the phased roll-out: companies with turnover > EUR 8M must issue and invoice system from 2021, all other operators from 2024-2025 (regulatory deadlines extended); SII data entry remains the primary real-time fiscal clearance channel for IVA, while physical invoicing is governed by RD 1619/2012.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under ART. 21 Ley 37/1992, exports of goods to third countries or destinations outside the EU customs territory are zero-rated (exempt with credit/0% IVA) provided the goods physically leave the EU within 3 months of dispatch (art. 21.1), under the exporter's customs export declaration (DUA/SAD). Condition: the Spanish SL must be the exporter (the holder/consignor of the customs declaration) and dispatch/transportation must be effected to a destination outside the Community territory (outside EU, or under the customs free-circuit regimes: customs warehouses, free zones, inward processing). The claim requires the simultaneous completion of the underlying commercial invoice with the export declaration and proof of physical departure in support; professional certificate by the customs office if lost (per Art. 21.2). Zero-rating likewise applies to (i) intra-EU supplies of goods intracomunitarias transferred to VAT-registered customers under the reverse-charge (Art. 21.3) and (ii) services under ART. 25 (transformation-OUTWARD processing and International sales commission for exported goods; a processing or disposed goods service abroad satisfies other interfaces and supportive proof requirements for offshore services provided that the recipient is established outside the EU and the service is not connected with Spanish real property).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Código de aduanas: Declaración de Exportación (DUA) / Single Administrative Document (SAD) with requirement for electronic export clearance via ICEX/DMS - Export declarations are filled through DUA in the electronic 'CEDA' (borrador) with the Expediente de Exportación DE (Surveillance) and confirmation of exit
Bill of Lading (Conocimiento de embarque / Declaración Marítima de Carga) or Air Waybill / CMR (for freight land) / SMGS waybill and packing list (lista de bultos), if dispatch inland

Inward Remittance Certificate (Justificante de transferencia bancaria de entrada de divisas - Confirmación de pago SWIFT/MT103, with bank credit advice referenced to the invoice); complementary Proof of Export certificate issued by the customs office / Agencia Tributaria (Certificado de Exportación, 'ECAA'), when queried

Commercial Pro-forma & Final Tax Invoice (Factura comercial con cláusula IVA exenta ART. 21); plus the corresponding customs export file (expediente de exportación) and official receipt for logistics and destination-entry customs stamps
Alternative documentary proof for the three-month rule: EUR.1 / EUR-MED certificate details (preferential origin) or certificate of shipment if customs verified
Export Intrastat filing (modelo N-I-D-28) and supporting freight/insurance invoices to evidence cross-border transit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audit units and the Oficina Nacional de Investigación del Fraude (ONIF) scrutinize zero-rated exports under ART. 21 for documentary evidence of exit (prueba de salida). If the export is not substantiated, the invoice is recharacterized as a domestic supply subject to 21% IVA (plus IVA-ES→ other Member State identification under the reverse-charge), with the consequent liability for (i) IVA not charged (principal tax debt), (ii) late-payment interest (interés de demora, Ley 58/2003 ART. 26), (iii) a proportional penalty under ART. 184 Ley 58/2003 of 50% of the omitted tax (reduced grade: 50%; if total omission exceeds EUR 3,000 or a sustained pattern, elevated quotes of 75-100% apply; public attack for fraud (ANVSA ART. 46/2016) 150%); additionally (iv) penalties for false or non-existent export documentation under ART. 201 (sanción por dato falso, EUR 300-1,500 and per false data, or 100% where evasion exceeds EUR 120,000); (v) the clawback of previously refunded IVA/IMV for which the record was used as ground for export zero-rating (duplicative repayment, with rectification under ART. 120.3 GST); and (vi) criminal liability under ART. 306 Código Penal (delito contra la Hacienda Pública) where the defrauded IVA exceeds EUR 120,000 or the facilitative offense is corroborated, with prison terms of 1-5 years and fines, plus disqualification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) within the Eurosystem, jointly with the European Central Bank; the Dirección General de Transacciones Exteriores (DGTE) of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation is the competent administrative authority for foreign investment and balance-of-payments reporting under Royal Decree 1816/1991.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies full convertibility for the euro on both current and capital account transactions. There are no general exchange controls or restrictions on profit remittance by a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada to non-resident shareholders. Dividend distributions to non-residents are subject to Spanish non-resident income tax withholding at 19% unless reduced by an applicable double-tax treaty; this is a tax obligation, not a foreign-exchange control. Banks may require documentary support for statistical reporting and AML source-of-funds verification, but there is no prior FX licensing or conversion mandate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender of export proceeds applies in Spain. Exporters may retain euros or foreign currency in freely convertible bank accounts, whether in Spain or abroad. Export receipts must be reported for balance-of-payments statistics to the Bank of Spain when they exceed EUR 50,000 per transaction or aggregate thresholds, using the T-1/declaración de transacciones exteriores filing mechanism. Conversion of foreign-currency receipts to euros is voluntary and subject to normal commercial banking terms.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium for offshore digital EMI providers. Under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and Spanish transposition, only EEA-authorised or passport-licensed EMIs may lawfully provide payment accounts in euros to Spanish residents. Offshore EMIs without an EEA authorisation cannot provide Spanish IBANs or operate as primary clearing accounts for local operational cash flow. For a medium-risk IVD manufacturer with cross-border trade, a full-authorised Spanish bank is strongly preferred; an EEA-passported EMI may be acceptable only as a supplemental collection gateway, not as the main treasury clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is partially permitted in Spain. Non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners may undergo video-identification using a Bank of Spain approved electronic identification process, but in practice Spanish relationship banks require at least one director or an appointed local agent with a Spanish NIE to attend a physical interview when the company has foreign ownership and is engaged in medical-device manufacturing. A physical presence visit to the bank branch or notary is strongly recommended during incorporation to obtain the corporate NIF and bank certification without delay.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholder structure with multi-jurisdiction holding companies or opaque ownership in low-tax jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organisational chart, certificate of incorporation and good standing of each direct and indirect shareholder, UBO register extract with percentage breakdown, audited financial statements of intermediate shareholders, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds letters, tax residence certificates, and a copy of the shareholders' agreement or capital injection resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IVD manufacturing classified as enhanced-scrutiny due to cross-border distributors, high transaction velocity with Latin American counterparties, and complex export invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish AEMPS medical device registration or CE marking certificate, ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 certificates, manufacturing site inspection report, signed commercial distribution and supply contracts, proforma invoices and customs declarations, track-and-trace shipping evidence, and a detailed business plan demonstrating the commercial rationale for the treasury flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments received from or destined to jurisdictions perceived as higher-risk for money laundering or with sanctions exposure, or frequent use of third-party payment intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML/CFT policies and procedures, transaction monitoring and sanctions screening logs covering SWIFT messages and SEPA files, customer and supplier due diligence questionnaires, periodic PEP and adverse-media screening reports, copies of export delivery documents, and a declared purpose for each significant transaction family.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionately large or early capital injection relative to the paid-in share capital stated in the notarial deed, or rapid repatriation as dividends.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed of incorporation and restated articles, capital increase resolution registered at the Commercial Registry, bank confirmation of share capital payment, projected cash flow and funding plan, transfer pricing documentation, and a dividend distribution resolution with corporate tax payment proof.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital routes: non-resident shareholders remit euro-denominated funds via SWIFT MT103 or, where the remitter is in the SEPA zone, a SEPA CT with ISO 20022 pain.001. Payment must identify the Spanish SL as beneficiary with NIF code and clearly state 'Direct investment in Spanish subsidiary - capital account'. For statistical compliance with the Bank of Spain, the foreign-investment declaration must be filed under the Dirección General de Transacciones Exteriores framework using the 'Inversión exterior directa' classification, and the receiving bank must receive a certified copy of the capital increase deed and the Commercial Registry filing. The bank will perform source-of-funds verification for the full amount; if the capital is remitted in USD, it is converted to EUR at the bank's open market rate with no FX control restriction. Beneficiary bank must release escrowed funds only after the notarial deed and regulatory licence (Spanish AEMPS registration for IVD manufacturing) are presented.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing rails: euro-denominated supplier and trade payments are cleared via SEPA/TARGET2 and SWIFT MT103 messages; for high-value or documentary export transactions to Latin America and non-EEA markets, the preferred rail is an irrevocable commercial letter of credit confirmed or advised through the Spanish bank's correspondent network, using SWIFT MT700 series for issuance, MT707 for amendments, and MT710/MT720 as applicable. Trade settlements for medical-device components require the presentation of commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, AEO certificate where available, and customs export declaration. Repatriation of export proceeds from non-EU buyers may be received via SWIFT MT103 into the same treasury account; amounts over EUR 50,000 must be captured in the periodic Bank of Spain balance-of-payments reporting file. For intra-group transactions, transfer pricing documentation must be maintained to satisfy anti-BEPS substance requirements and to support the clearing rails used.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD outright forward contracts with an EU-authorised credit institution for trade-receivable conversion
Spot-forward FX swaps and tom-next swaps to manage intra-month euro-liquidity from USD-denominated IVD distributor collections
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for USD/EUR treasury liabilities or long-term lease financing

Non-deliverable forwards for emerging-market currencies (e.g. LATAM currencies) only where the underlying trade exposure meets hedge effectiveness tests and an offshore deliverable market is unavailable

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard Spanish Corporate Income Tax rate. Eligible newly incorporated companies generally apply 15% during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory exclusions. Reduced rates may apply to qualifying micro-enterprises and small enterprises under transitional rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying research and development expenditure may benefit from a 25% deduction, increased to 42% for the excess over the average of the preceding two years, with an additional 17% deduction for qualifying R&D personnel costs. Qualifying technological innovation may receive a 12% deduction. The patent box regime may reduce qualifying net income from certain patents and protected intangible assets by 60%, subject to the modified nexus approach. Capitalisation and employment-related incentives may apply to qualifying enterprises. The general tax loss carryforward is indefinite, subject to annual utilization limits generally linked to turnover: 70%, 50%, or 25% of the pre-loss taxable base for larger taxpayers, with a generally available minimum offset of EUR 1 million. Tax losses remain subject to anti-abuse and change-of-control restrictions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite; Spain does not impose a general five-year expiry period. Annual offset limitations apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where available, or an authorized representative system. Related-party transactions and other tax information may require associated schedules and supplementary forms.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within the 25 calendar days immediately following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year company ending on 31 December, the usual filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the last day is not a business day, the applicable electronic filing calendar rules extend the deadline to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number, registered office, tax period, legal form, accounting currency, activity classification, and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not substituted for the Spanish SL. The SL files using its own Spanish tax identification number and Spanish tax residence status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Balance sheet and profit-and-loss account sections
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting assets, liabilities, equity, turnover, operating income, operating expenses, finance result, extraordinary items, and accounting profit or loss, reconciled to the statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amounts of foreign parent transactions must be recorded in the Spanish entity's accounts and translated under applicable Spanish accounting rules. Foreign parent accounting figures are not directly reported unless they form part of the SL's books.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent differences, temporary differences, nondeductible expenses, tax depreciation adjustments, provisions, impairment adjustments, exempt income, and other accounting-to-tax reconciliations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-law deductions or exemptions are unavailable unless recognized under Spanish law or an applicable treaty. Payments to non-residents require separate withholding and deductibility analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal depreciation of plant, machinery, laboratory equipment, analyzers, tooling, software, and other fixed assets using approved methods and statutory useful-life limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imported equipment must be capitalized by the Spanish SL at the appropriate tax basis, including directly attributable acquisition costs. Parent-company depreciation cannot be claimed by the SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Research, development, innovation, and investment incentive schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying R&D, technological innovation, patent box income, environmental investment, employment incentives, and other applicable tax credits or reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign group R&D costs are not automatically eligible. The SL must demonstrate that the qualifying activity, expenditure, and statutory nexus are attributable to Spain or otherwise meet Spanish requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening tax losses, losses generated in the current period, utilized losses, remaining balances, annual utilization limitation, and EUR 1 million minimum offset threshold where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a foreign parent or sister company cannot be used by the SL unless a legally available Spanish tax consolidation regime or other specific provision applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions with related entities, shareholders, directors, group companies, permanent establishments, and entities in low-tax or non-cooperative jurisdictions, including transaction type and aggregate value.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border purchases, royalties, management fees, financing, guarantees, contract manufacturing, and technical support from non-residents must be reported and supported by arm's-length documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish withholding tax suffered, installment payments made under Modelo 202, foreign tax credits, and other payments on account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding is creditable only within Spanish statutory and treaty limits and normally requires official evidence of payment and income attribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Final tax liability and payment details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross liability, tax credits, payments on account, amount payable or refundable, bank account, direct debit instruction, or payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder's bank account does not replace the Spanish SL's filing and payment obligations. Any refund must be supported by the Spanish return and eligible Spanish bank or payment details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic signature, authorized filer identification, submission receipt, payment confirmation, and supporting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign director or shareholder generally requires a Spanish electronic certificate, recognized representative, or Spanish tax agent with authority to file.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment of an assessed amount generally triggers a voluntary-period surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay up to 12 months; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus statutory late-payment interest. Late filing without a payable amount may attract a fixed penalty generally ranging from EUR 100 to EUR 200, subject to statutory reduction and circumstances. Failure to file, inaccurate filing, concealment, or fraudulent conduct may trigger penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the improperly unpaid or improperly obtained amount, with interest and collection costs. Failure to make Modelo 202 installment payments may create a principal tax debt, interest, and enforcement surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Corporate Income Tax installment payment, submitted electronically through AEAT. The installment is generally calculated under the prior-year liability method or, where elected or required, the current-period accounting-result method.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly installment schedule; normally due in April, October, and December
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December; electronic direct-debit deadlines may be earlier under AEAT payment-calendar rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish tax identification number, legal name, tax period, installment number, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL files in its own name. Non-resident ownership does not remove the SL's installment obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-period Corporate Income Tax liability or current-period accounting and tax result, depending on the elected statutory method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign group financial results are excluded unless legally included in a Spanish tax group or directly attributable to the SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Percentage applied, deductions, credits, prior installments, and final amount payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are not automatically available against installment payments and require Spanish statutory support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payment reference, direct debit or NRC payment code, electronic signature, and submission receipt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent should fund the SL in a manner documented as equity or debt and consistent with transfer-pricing and corporate-law requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-payment produces an enforceable tax debt, statutory interest, and collection surcharges. Late or incorrect filing may produce fixed or proportional penalties depending on the resulting tax shortfall and taxpayer conduct.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, Informative declaration of related-party transactions and transactions involving jurisdictions classified as non-cooperative, filed electronically through AEAT when statutory thresholds or reporting conditions are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December year-end, the usual deadline is the following November.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Counterparty, country, relationship, transaction category, transaction amount, and valuation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report qualifying cross-border group transactions using the Spanish SL's statutory related-party classification and transaction values.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate amounts by transaction type and counterparty, including recurring purchases, royalties, services, financing, guarantees, and asset transfers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aggregate recurring transactions consistently and retain reconciliations to the general ledger, invoices, contracts, customs records, and withholding returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions with persons or entities resident in jurisdictions listed under applicable Spanish non-cooperative jurisdiction rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Additional scrutiny, beneficial-owner evidence, economic-purpose documentation, and withholding analysis are required for such transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic filing identity, declaration status, and submission receipt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The filing must be made by the SL or its duly authorized Spanish electronic representative.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to submit or materially inaccurate reporting may generate statutory informative-return penalties, generally calculated by omitted or incorrect data, subject to minimum amounts and statutory caps. The underlying transaction remains subject to transfer-pricing adjustment and possible tax penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 216, withholding and payment on account for income obtained in Spain by non-residents, and Modelo 296, annual informative summary of such withholdings, filed electronically through AEAT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 216 is generally due within the first 20 calendar days of April, July, October, and January for the preceding quarter. Modelo 296 is generally due in January for the preceding calendar year, subject to the applicable AEAT calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recipient name, tax residence, identification number, address, income type, and treaty-status data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain a current certificate of tax residence before applying treaty relief or an exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross royalty, interest, service, rental, dividend, or other Spanish-source payment and domestic or treaty withholding rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not apply a reduced treaty rate solely on the basis of a contractual statement. Retain tax residence, beneficial ownership, and eligibility evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal exemption, European Union exemption, treaty article, or reduced rate applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document EU parent-subsidiary, interest-and-royalty, treaty, or domestic exemptions before payment whenever practicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax withheld, payment reference, and aggregate quarterly or annual totals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL remains liable for withholding even if the contract allocates the economic cost to the non-resident recipient.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold or remit may create primary liability for the unpaid withholding, late-payment interest, and proportional tax penalties. Late informative filings may incur fixed penalties, increased where data is omitted, incorrect, or submitted after an AEAT requirement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish resident company to a non-resident, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU or European Economic Area parent may be exempt under the Spanish implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring a minimum 5% participation, a minimum one-year holding period or commitment, qualifying legal form and taxation, and anti-abuse and beneficial-ownership conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a tax residence certificate issued by the recipient's tax authority and verify the relevant treaty article, beneficial ownership, anti-abuse provisions, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose considerations where applicable, and participation conditions. The Spanish SL should retain the certificate, ownership chain, board and dividend resolutions, payment records, and evidence of treaty eligibility. Apply the treaty rate at source only where Spanish administrative requirements are satisfied; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and allow the recipient to pursue a refund through the applicable non-resident tax procedure. Certificates should be renewed according to their validity period and before future distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Spanish non-resident withholding rate is generally 24% for royalties and interest, reduced to 19% for residents of the European Union, Iceland, and Norway under applicable domestic rules. A tax treaty may reduce the rate, including to zero in specific cases. Qualifying associated companies resident in EU Member States may receive exemption for interest and royalties under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, generally requiring qualifying legal form and taxation, a minimum 25% direct or indirect relationship, a minimum one-year holding period or commitment, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse compliance. Service fees require separate source, permanent-establishment, treaty, and business-activity analysis.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spain generally does not require full related-party documentation for transactions of the same type and valuation method with the same related party not exceeding EUR 250,000 in the tax period. Separate lower thresholds generally apply to certain real-estate transactions and transactions involving intangible assets. Local-file requirements apply subject to statutory exemptions and simplified documentation rules. A Spanish master file is generally required for entities belonging to a group, with an important exemption where the group is below the applicable EUR 45 million net turnover threshold. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. These thresholds do not eliminate the arm's-length requirement or the obligation to maintain evidence supporting material transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no standalone regime titled Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore-jurisdiction ESR frameworks. Nevertheless, Spanish anti-abuse rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, the anti-simulation doctrine, beneficial-ownership principles, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest-limitation rules, principal-purpose analysis, and EU anti-abuse standards require genuine commercial substance. The SL should maintain Spanish decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or controlled facilities where commercially appropriate, manufacturing and quality systems, inventory and logistics control, risk assumption, technical competence, independent governance, and contemporaneous records. A conduit company receiving royalties, interest, management fees, or dividends without functions, assets, risks, and beneficial ownership is high risk.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.industry_specific_transfer_pricing_contr: For automated point-of-care IVD manufacturing, document product design ownership, regulatory and quality responsibilities, batch-release functions, warranty exposure, inventory risk, contract manufacturing terms, tooling ownership, software and algorithm rights, validation costs, distributor margins, and allocation of clinical, regulatory, and post-market surveillance activities. Intercompany royalty rates and technical-service charges should be supported by benefit analysis, DEMPE functions, comparable evidence, and Spanish withholding treatment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent Corporate Income Tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating expenses, maintaining parallel accounts, falsely claiming R&D deductions, or deliberately understating taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid or improperly refunded tax, plus interest and collection costs. If the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal tax fraud may apply, generally carrying imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or organized conduct, may carry imprisonment of two to six years and a fine of two to six times the amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil liability for restitution and fines, and subsidiary liability for unpaid tax where statutory control, participation, or negligent management conditions are met. Travel restrictions or precautionary asset measures may be ordered in criminal or enforcement proceedings; imprisonment follows only a final criminal conviction and applicable judicial process.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False transfer pricing, concealed related-party distributions, or non-arm's-length intercompany charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using unsupported royalties, management fees, financing, guarantees, procurement charges, or loss allocations to shift profit outside Spain or disguise dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may make a primary transfer-pricing adjustment, secondary adjustment, interest assessment, and administrative penalty. Material documentation failures may attract penalties calculated by omitted or incorrect data or, where tax is underpaid, proportional penalties generally within the tax-penalty ranges applicable to the conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil damages, tax subsidiary liability, and criminal exposure where the arrangement forms part of intentional tax fraud. Corporate separateness is not an absolute defense against proven fraud, simulation, abuse, or personal participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper dividend, interest, or royalty withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying treaty or EU exemptions without a valid residence certificate, beneficial ownership, participation, holding-period, anti-abuse, or substance evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish SL may be assessed for the unpaid withholding, late-payment interest, and proportional tax penalties. Treaty relief may be denied and the recipient may be required to seek recovery through a refund procedure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary liability where failure to withhold resulted from deliberate or negligent management. Fraudulent withholding certificates or sham ownership structures may generate criminal tax exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, sham residence, or beneficial-ownership abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an entity with nominal directors, no operational capacity, circular funds, artificial contracts, or conduit ownership to obtain treaty benefits or deduct payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Benefits may be denied under anti-abuse, simulation, principal-purpose, and beneficial-ownership principles. Tax, interest, penalties, withholding assessments, and transaction recharacterization may follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who direct or knowingly facilitate the arrangement may incur civil, administrative, or criminal liability. Courts may disregard separate legal personality in cases of fraud, abuse of rights, or unlawful asset diversion; precautionary travel or asset restrictions may be imposed by judicial order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining off-book inventory, falsifying production costs, backdating invoices, destroying accounting records, or misrepresenting laboratory equipment and development expenditure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, bookkeeping and tax penalties, loss of deductions, interest, and possible criminal accounting or tax-fraud proceedings may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for creditor and shareholder losses, tax debts under statutory conditions, insolvency-related liability, and criminal offenses involving falsification or fraudulent accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party funds, disguising beneficial owners, failing customer due diligence, ignoring unusual wire transfers, or failing to report suspicious activity where the SL is a regulated obliged entity or acts through regulated counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious infringements can produce substantial fines, including amounts linked to the transaction, annual turnover, or statutory maximums, together with public or private reprimands, temporary suspension, and management disqualification. Exact exposure depends on classification and the regulated status of the obligated person.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and de facto managers may be individually sanctioned or prosecuted for knowing participation, gross negligence, obstruction, or laundering. Asset freezing, travel restrictions, and imprisonment may apply in criminal proceedings after judicial determination.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, VAT, product-regulatory, and medical-device misclassification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underdeclaring customs value, misclassifying IVD cartridges or analyzers, claiming unsupported import VAT treatment, falsifying origin, or selling devices without required EU and Spanish conformity, registration, traceability, or post-market controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs and VAT reassessments, import duties, interest, administrative fines, seizure, market withdrawal, suspension of activities, and product-regulatory sanctions may apply. Serious product-safety breaches may trigger criminal liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil product liability, regulatory disqualification, tax liability, and criminal exposure for intentional trafficking, falsification, or knowing distribution of unsafe or non-compliant devices.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain transfer-pricing, accounting, or tax records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing local file, master file, invoices, technical-benefit evidence, intercompany agreements, customs reconciliations, or records required to substantiate deductions and treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Specific documentation penalties may apply per omitted, inaccurate, or incomplete data, subject to statutory minimums and maximums. The absence of documentation also increases the risk of direct tax adjustments and broader penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur administrative or subsidiary tax liability where recordkeeping failures are attributable to intentional or negligent management. Criminal liability requires additional elements such as fraud, concealment, or participation in an offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal profit distribution and insolvency prejudice
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, ignoring mandatory reserves, stripping assets before creditor payment, or repaying shareholder loans while the company is insolvent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Improper distributions may require restitution, interest, corporate-law sanctions, and insolvency clawback. Directors may be subject to insolvency qualification consequences, disqualification, loss of rights against the estate, and liability for the insolvency deficit in appropriate cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal restitution, damages, disqualification from administration, and criminal liability for insolvency crimes or asset concealment. Judicial asset-preservation and travel measures may be available in insolvency or criminal proceedings.
